subject: Product-slice indemnity limits and evidence path (MSA v3 redlines)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elaine Turner <elaine@heracleshealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Product-slice indemnity limits and evidence path (MSA v3 redlines)

Elaine —

Following our procurement thread, attaching MSA_v3_redline.docx with the approach the account team and I discussed. High level: because Heracles is buying a bundle of capabilities (core infra + several optional connectors and an integration layer), we proposed splitting indemnity exposure by product slice rather than one blanket exposure across the entire enterprise order.

Why we think this helps both sides:
- Limits map to the order form line item (so a single bad outcome for a peripheral connector can’t consume the platform cap).
- For IP infringement / third-party claims we propose a tiered "waterfall":
  * Tier 1 (Core platform): Redwood to defend and indemnify for third-party IP claims tied to our model/service. Cap = 3x monthly committed spend (order-form).
  * Tier 2 (Optional connectors / customer-configured modules): limited indemnity — Redwood will defend only for claims arising from the parts we ship; customer owns risk for their custom logic or customer-provided models.
  * Escrow trigger: if aggregate liability for a single incident > $250,000 for regulated healthcare accounts, an escrow-and-custodian mechanism kicks in pending resolution.

Operational asks for Heracles: a 30-day notice window on alleged claims, named evidence custodian (ops contact), and a short evidence checklist we can use to triage (attached).

Can we schedule 30 minutes Thursday to walk the doc with legal? If you prefer, I can loop in Marcus and Kimberly to go through specific language live.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: MSA_v3_redline.docx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Product-slice indemnity limits and evidence path (MSA v3 redlines)

Tessa — thanks for sharing the draft. A few internal legal comments we should propose in the call so commercial has a firm position: 

1) Notice and Cooperation
- Keep customer notice short (30 days) but add cure window for Redwood to investigate (we recommend 60 days to assemble technical evidence).

2) Defense Control and Settlement
- Redwood should have the right to assume defense for Tier 1 platform claims (we will control counsel selection) with an obligation to consult the customer on material decisions; settlements that impose ongoing obligations on the customer should require customer consent.

3) Escrow & Thresholds
- Escrow trigger as proposed is reasonable for healthcare customers; suggest a defined custodian and a process timeline (we've attached an evidence_checklist.xlsx).

4) Cap by product slice
- Cap expressed as multiple of monthly committed spend in the order form fine, but ensure language allows per-incident aggregation only for claims tied to the same product slice.

5) Open-source / Third-party component carveouts
- Add explicit exclusion for claims arising from customer-customized OSS components where customer modified or combined the code.

6) Insurance/involvement of carrier
- If claim exceeds the cap or triggers escrow, we should be able to require insurer engagement and expedite subrogation efforts.

I attached a redline with proposed language snippets. Happy to present these on the Thursday call; Marcus, can you review the escrow custodian suggestion and confirm commercial operational feasibility?

—Kimberly Park
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: MSA_v3_redline.docx, evidence_checklist.xlsx
From: John Smythe <john.smythe@heracleslegal.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:27:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Product-slice indemnity limits and evidence path (MSA v3 redlines)

Tessa / Kimberly —

Thanks for the redline. A few immediate items from Heracles counsel: 

- Notice timing: 30 days is aggressive for complex patent or third-party claims — we need at least 45 calendar days to notify impacted downstream parties and pull internal evidence. Can you accept 45 days?

- Insurer participation: Heracles requires the ability to require insurer involvement (and reasonable cooperation from Redwood) where a claim exceeds the stated cap or triggers escrow. We will also ask for a representation that Redwood currently maintains commercial general liability and tech E&O with limits at least $5M.

- Reverse-indemnity concern: if the claim arises from Redwood’s transformation of customer data (e.g., model fine-tuning on customer-provided datasets), Heracles needs clearer language that Redwood accepts exposure and will defend—otherwise we will push for a reverse indemnity (i.e., Redwood reimburses us).

- Evidence custody: Heracles agrees to name an ops custodian but requests parity in access to forensic artifacts (logs, model inputs) for the duration of the investigation with appropriate privacy safeguards.

Can we lock in a call Friday morning (our time) to work through the escrow threshold and the reverse-indemnity language?

Regards,
John Smythe
Partner, Heracles Legal
Heracles Health
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elaine Turner <elaine@heracleshealth.com>, John Smythe <john.smythe@heracleslegal.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Product-slice indemnity limits and evidence path (MSA v3 redlines)

Elaine and John — appreciate the fast turnaround and practical asks. Proposed compromise to take to procurement/legal teams: 

1) Defense split by product origin
- Redwood will defend/indemnify for third-party IP claims that specifically arise from the platform/model outputs and the software we ship (Tier 1).
- For customer-provided models, connectors, or customer-authored code that materially contributed to the alleged infringement, Heracles will defend; Redwood will offer limited reimbursement for reasonable litigation costs where we can show contribution.

2) Escrow threshold / regulated accounts
- For Heracles (regulated healthcare customer) we will lower the escrow trigger to $250,000 per-incident. Custodian to be named in order form; funds held subject to a short dispute process (30 days).

3) Notice & Evidence
- Accept 45 days for initial notice. Redwood will require timely cooperation; we will agree to reasonable parity access to forensic logs with privacy redactions. We will add an evidence checklist to the MSA and a joint evidence-preservation call template.

4) Insurer engagement
- If claim exceeds the cap or escrow is triggered, both parties will engage carriers and cooperate in subrogation; Redwood confirms we maintain primary tech E&O limits of at least $5M (policy details to be provided).

Next steps: Kimberly will circulate a revised redline reflecting these bullets and a draft escrow custodian clause by EOD Monday. Tessa will update the HubSpot DEAL-8792 record and send a DocuSign placeholder for the order-form addendum.

Marcus Lin
VP Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
